mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong residential construction demand, which typically precedes higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.10% for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary easing that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS has been below 0.10% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates strong demand supported by accommodative policy, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 1% and FEDFUNDS decreases by at least 0.05 percentage points month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 7.5%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is above 7.5% and declines by at least 0.2 percentage points month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 7.5% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE has been above 7.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates inflationary pressures from a tight labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed may tighten policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL increases by at least 0.2% and UNRATE decreases by at least 0.1 percentage points month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 annual growth > 2.5%), a decline in the real GDP growth rate (GDPC1) signals an economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 annual growth rate declines below 2.5%.
